name: Exo-Dermis
description:
Exo-Dermis emerged from the practice of composing sound specifically for augmented skin receptors and subdermal haptic implants, treating the entire body as a listening surface rather than privileging the ears. Composers encode vibration signatures, pressure gradients, and temperature-adjacent sensations into layered audio-haptic scores, producing music that is felt architecturally across the flesh before it is consciously processed as melody or rhythm. The effect is deeply disorienting to the unaugmented, who hear only a sparse and eerily quiet drone, while augmented listeners experience a full somatic symphony.

Originating in the body-modification communes of the Sub-7 industrial corridors circa 2198, Exo-Dermis quickly gained traction among manual laborers whose hearing had been damaged by factory environments but whose haptic implants remained functional. Labels distribute the format as dual-channel haptic-audio files, and live performances are notorious for audiences visibly flinching, swaying, or weeping in response to stimuli that observers cannot perceive.
creator: various
tier_availability: Tiers 4-7; haptic implant required for full experience; limited audio-only versions available higher
legality: Legal in most districts; Tier 1-2 residential blocks restrict live performances citing public disturbance
audience: Augmented laborers, body-modification subcultures, chronic noise-exposure workers, somatic therapy patients
cultural_impact: Exo-Dermis fundamentally challenged the assumption that music is an auditory art form, forcing regulatory bodies to rewrite performance licensing to account for non-acoustic sensory broadcasts. It created an unexpected solidarity between low-tier augmented workers and high-tier biohackers who both claimed the genre as their own, generating one of the rare cross-tier cultural arguments that ended in shared ownership rather than appropriation conflict. Medical practitioners have also noted its therapeutic adoption among patients with auditory nerve damage.
story_hooks: A banned Exo-Dermis performance is being held in a sealed factory floor; attendees are going in with calibrated implants but someone has tampered with the haptic frequencies to dangerous resonance levels
An unaugmented detective must investigate a murder at an Exo-Dermis concert where the only witnesses experienced the event entirely through their skin and cannot describe what they saw
A composer claims their new Exo-Dermis score contains a hidden message embedded in the haptic layer — corporate interests want it suppressed before anyone decodes it
